fact: Appleby, a law firm, describes the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act 2026 as enacted Mauritian law that recognises electronic signatures, electronic transferable records and contracts formed by automated message systems, amending the existing Electronic Transactions framework; no commencement date is given, and the as_of date is the article's published date.

Act No. 5 of 2026, the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act, was passed by the National Assembly on 19 May 2026 and assented to by the President on 25 May 2026; it comes into operation on a date to be fixed by Proclamation, different sections possibly on different dates, and the document gives no commencement date.

The ICT minister, speaking on 29 July 2026, referred to amendments to the Electronic Transactions Act 2006 meant to modernise digital commerce frameworks and strengthen consumer protection, which treats the 2006 Act as existing law; the document gives no date for the Act's entry into force and does not say the amendments are passed.
